_about: Ireland Readiness Checklist: questions, options and rules (brief, Fix 6b). Read by the website AND by the notify-waitlist Edge Function, which recomputes the items itself from the saved answers so nobody can put their own text into an email sent from our domain. Edit wording here only. An item with no 'when' is shown to everyone.

questions.prompt: What are you planning to study?
Which country do you live in?
When do you hope to start?
Does your chosen course follow on from your previous study or work?
Have you taken an English language test (such as IELTS, PTE or TOEFL)?
options: Not sure if I need one

questions.prompt: Is your passport valid for your full planned stay in Ireland?

items.text: Narrow down to 2–3 Irish courses that build on what you've studied so far.
Be ready to explain clearly how your chosen course connects to your previous study or career plans.
Many Irish courses recruit on a rolling basis, so applying early helps. Aim to apply in the next few months.

in: Not sure if I need one

items.text: Check whether your course needs an English test, and make sure your result will still be valid when you apply.
Check your passport's expiry date and renew early if needed. Renewals can take weeks.
Plan your study budget together early, and check the official requirements on irishimmigration.ie.
Gather your academic transcripts and certificates in one place.
If you've ever been refused a visa for any country, you'll need to declare it when you apply.
Only apply and pay through official Irish channels. Visa applications go through the official online system (AVATS).
